title: Tenant fanout caps and model-fallback playbook for GPU drain events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During the 2026-03-08 hosted API capacity incident we observed rapid GPU pool exhaustion driven by a single customer performing high-fanout inference patterns (same input fan-out to many model variants) combined with a regression in the admission scoring that overly favored long-lived KV-cache heavy sessions. The result was sustained GPU queue buildup, elevated tail latency, and a spike in 5xx errors for other tenants.
decision_log: Adopt tenant-level fanout cap (default 8 concurrent model forks) to reduce simultaneous model replication demands on GPU pools — trade-off: some large customers need explicit quota increases via dedicated capacity.

Implement a two-stage admission hysteresis: soft-threshold (queue_len > 60% capacity) triggers admission score multiplier; hard-threshold (queue_len > 85%) forces model-fallback or preemptive eviction of non-critical batches.

Route overflow to CPU-only cheap model variants for best-effort requests when GPU latency SLOs are at risk — trade-off: reduced quality for a subset of requests but keeps system availability for high-priority traffic.
Avoid aggressive global autoscale until per-tenant shaping is in place to prevent perpetual scale-churn and cost blowouts observed in previous incidents.
action_items: (Owner: Diego) Implement tenant_fanout_limit configurable at account level with default=8 and enforcement at admission service (estimate: 3 pts).
(Owner: Priya Shah) Add admission_hysteresis windowing: 30s lookback + exponential backoff multiplier for admission scoring (estimate: 2 pts).
(Owner: Rui Chen) Add model_fallback route: GPU->CPU variant mapping and automated routing when pool queue exceeds hard-threshold; include cost/quality telemetry (estimate: 5 pts).
(Owner: DevOps) Add per-model and per-tenant queue histograms + 95/99/999 latency heatmaps to Console and alert when tenant queue_share > 40% of pool for 2m (estimate: 2 pts).
(Owner: QA) Build synthetic fanout chaos test that reproduces previous pattern and gates the rollout (estimate: 3 pts).
(Owner: SRE) Update runbook: include new prewarm policy, fallback activation steps, and rollback instructions; add playbook snippet to paging flow (estimate: 1 pt).
(Owner: Legal/PM) Customer outreach: notify impacted customers with mitigations and recommend Dedicated for sustained high-fanout workloads (owner: Claire, estimate: 1 pt).

notes: Key trade-offs: conservative per-tenant caps protect multi-tenant pools but create a path for customers to request Dedicated capacity. Model-fallback preserves availability at the cost of quality for best-effort paths. Hysteresis prevents oscillations that previously caused autoscaler thrash.
acceptance_criteria: Implement fanout limit enforcement and ability to request quota overrides via support flow.
Admission hysteresis active with documented knobs; verify queue_len oscillation < 15% during synthetic test.
Model fallback successfully routes >90% of overflow requests to CPU variant with failure rate <1% and captured quality metrics.
Dashboards show per-tenant queue_share and new alerts fire on >40% sustained share.
Runbook updated and on-call trained on new playbook before broad rollout.
